The right hemisphere opens at the Sylvian fissure (the first slider): the lips moved apart 6 mm up and 6 mm down, the rest following as rigidly as possible; and its frontal lobe lifts off the orbital roof (the second slider: 8 mm along a corridor from the anterior clinoid process forward to the frontal pole, the front of the insula with it; in the lateral supraorbital view 12 mm along that approach's corridor, out over the lateral orbital roof). In the interhemispheric view its medial surface is held 8 mm off the falx over the craniotomy's length, the medial wall and the callosum staying. Shapes, not a simulation of the tissue.
